ghost_placement.statement: Left ghost (theory: f = f^(0) + xi f_Delta) and right ghost (engine B: f = f^(0) + f_Delta xi) differ by f_Delta^left = (-1)^{|f_Delta|} f_Delta^right; for the degree -1 components (S^(1)(Delta), I^CT_Delta, F(Delta)) the sign flips uniformly, for the degree 0 component Ob(Delta) it does not.  All three groups define the arity-one vertex as J_Delta = S^(1)(Delta) - I^CT_Delta[eps] - F(Delta) with S^(1)(Delta) the explicit functional of ex:c2-dil, and Ob(Delta) as the local functional whose tree flow is lim Q W'_J(S^(1)(Delta) - I^CT_Delta); the equation Q W'_J(J_Delta) -> 0 contains no xi, so F(Delta) and Ob(Delta) = (Q + {I,-}) F(Delta) are the same functionals in all three conventions; only the global sign of the component is fixed by the normalisation "classical part = +{S^(1)(Delta),O}" (prop:c6-classical), used by all three.
ghost_placement.engine_A: component normalised so that the classical part is +2(E+w_O)O; J_Delta = S_M - I^CT_Delta - F_Delta (Y1b + CT = C_P(Pi_int - F_Delta, O))
ghost_placement.engine_B: right ghost: J = I - I^CT - F_0 + (S_M - I^CT_Delta - F(Delta)) xi
ghost_placement.theory: left ghost; J_Delta = S^(1)(Delta) - I^CT_Delta - hbar F_1(Delta); (Q+{I,-})hbar F_1(Delta) = Ob(Delta) (eq:d-F)
